nodes.label: v2 #5 Digest Profiles & HTML Report Card Plan
nodes.norm_label: v2 #5 digest profiles & html report card plan

nodes.label: v1.5 Phase 3 Real Easy/Nerd Modes Plan
nodes.norm_label: v1.5 phase 3 real easy/nerd modes plan

nodes.label: Client-Side Privacy Architecture
nodes.rationale: Privacy is a literal fact of the architecture, not a policy promise: no server, no database, no accounts, no network calls. Parsing and analysis run entirely in the browser (Web Worker); the only persistence is localStorage.

nodes.label: Fixed Linear Analysis Pipeline (analyze())
nodes.rationale: The whole analysis is a fixed, linear pipeline assembled at one seam (src/engine/analyze.ts) so the entire data flow reads in ~45 lines: decode -> parseCsv -> buildColumns -> normalize -> buildFps -> computeStats -> detectors -> buildVerdict -> buildDigest.

nodes.label: src/types.ts as Central Contract
nodes.rationale: Modules communicate only through shapes defined in src/types.ts; changing a type means touching multiple layers. Treat it as the central interface and read it before moving data between stages.

nodes.label: Windows-1252 Byte Decoding
nodes.rationale: HWiNFO logs are often Windows-1252, not UTF-8 (the degree sign in degC breaks naive UTF-8 readers). Always read as bytes and decode via parsing/decode; never read sample files as UTF-8 strings, including in tests.

nodes.label: Hardware Fingerprint Inference (No Hardware Database)
nodes.rationale: There is no hardware database. CPU/GPU/RAM models and laptop-vs-desktop are inferred from HWiNFO trailer rows and column-label heuristics in sensors/fingerprint.ts, falling back to a topology guess from core counts.

nodes.label: dGPU vs iGPU Section-Anchor Disambiguation
nodes.rationale: Column names collide between discrete and integrated GPUs; normalize.ts uses section anchors to assign each column and the first column to claim a key wins.

nodes.label: FPS Cap Detection Heuristic
nodes.rationale: FPS is treated as capped when ~80% of cleaned samples sit within +-1 of a candidate ceiling (common caps plus the highest measured value).

nodes.label: Web Worker Off-Main-Thread Analysis
nodes.rationale: Heavy parsing runs off the main thread: analyze.worker.ts is a thin wrapper around analyze(), driven by the useAnalysis hook which spawns the worker once and posts the file as bytes.

nodes.label: specsStore localStorage Persistence
nodes.rationale: specsStore.ts persists the editable specs card under key wtfps.specs.v1 and only restores saved specs when the CPU+GPU models match the new log, so one rig's log can't shadow another's.

nodes.label: Golden Integration Tests on Real Logs
nodes.rationale: Golden tests under src/engine/ run real logs from HWINFO samples/; the bar is every sample loads with no errors and no NaN.
nodes.norm_label: golden integration tests on real logs

nodes.label: Midnight Timestamp Crossing Correction
nodes.rationale: HWiNFO timestamps reset at midnight, so normalize.ts adds 24h to a negative time delta.

nodes.label: Copy Prompt for My LLM Digest
nodes.rationale: Signature feature: a compact, token-efficient digest (specs + percentile stats + plain-English events + editable goal line) — never the raw CSV — so any LLM can give sharp personalized tuning advice.
nodes.norm_label: copy prompt for my llm digest

nodes.label: Easy/Nerd Mode Toggle
nodes.rationale: Easy mode is short, plain, reassuring with one fix; Nerd mode is dense and exact with percentiles and 1%/5% lows. Same story, different depth.

nodes.label: Reactive Monitor Mascot
nodes.rationale: A monitor-creature whose mood (chill/concerned/panic) must always agree with the verdict health.

nodes.label: Four Detection Groups
nodes.rationale: v1 detects all four groups: thermal throttling, FPS-cap + cooling tips, CPU bottleneck, and power-limit/hotspot/RAM pressure.

nodes.label: Agent-Team Exclusive File Ownership Model
nodes.rationale: Lead + 2 teammates with exclusive write ownership per path; src/types.ts and stats/percentiles.ts are frozen pre-fan-out so two agents never write the same file or redefine the same interface. Build-time scaffolding, not an ongoing rule.

nodes.label: WTFPS v2 Roadmap (six plan-ready items)
nodes.rationale: Six items in strict order (compare/history, timelines, deeper diagnostics, specs breadth, digest profiles, packaging/a11y); each plan assumes the previous merged. Stretch: Tauri, live tail, share link.

nodes.label: Ambient Glass Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: A lit instrument room at night: fixed blue aurora behind everything, translucent floating panels, rationed real glass, dense data on solid metal.

nodes.label: Four-Tier Surface Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Atmosphere (bg+aurora+grain, never animated) -> translucent Panel (no backdrop blur) -> real Glass (exactly three surfaces, never more than 3 blur layers) -> Solid (all dense data). Never put dense data on a translucent surface.

nodes.label: Closed Glow List (exactly five glows)
nodes.rationale: Exactly five things glow: wordmark F, active mode tab, hero headline metric, warn/bad StatTile edge bars, the primary accent button. Nothing else, ever; one glowing accent CTA per surface.

nodes.label: Token-Only Styling Rule
nodes.rationale: Every color/font/space/radius/shadow/duration is a CSS variable in theme.css; component CSS may reference only var(--...) tokens — never a hardcoded hex, px font-size, or raw color.

nodes.label: Frozen UI Files Rule
nodes.rationale: Do not edit theme.css, cx.ts, the primitives/, or Mascot.tsx — import them; token or primitive changes go through the design lead.

nodes.label: Never Invent Numbers Principle
nodes.rationale: Never invent numbers the engine didn't produce; show an em dash or 'no framerate logged' when a value is absent.

nodes.label: Panel No-Blur Performance Policy
nodes.rationale: Behind ordinary panels is only a smooth fixed gradient + 5% grain; blurring a smooth gradient returns the same gradient, so alpha alone is visually identical and free. Real blur on 10-15 panels would force per-frame re-filtering during the rise entrance animation and jank.

nodes.label: Fixed Aurora + Film Grain Atmosphere
nodes.rationale: body::before/::after paint a static blue aurora and 5% film grain; the teal aurora color is atmosphere-only and must never appear on interactive elements.

nodes.label: Evidence Tiers: measured vs inferred
nodes.rationale: Every finding carries an evidence grade: measured (Tier 1: PresentMon busy/wait, latched limiter flags, per-frame-derived lows) vs inferred (Tier 2: utilization heuristics). The grade is shown in UI and digest; missing data triggers exact sensor guidance.

nodes.label: Windowed Gameplay Segmentation
nodes.rationale: The log is cut into ~5s windows classified gameplay/idle/loading; all verdicts and stats come from gameplay windows only, with coverage reported. Benchmark logs with no FPS classify as 'active workload' and never get a gaming verdict.

nodes.label: PresentMon GPU-Busy/Wait Limiter Classification
nodes.rationale: Per window dev = (frameTime - gpuBusy)/frameTime: <0.10 GPU-bound (unless power far below limit -> underutilized pathology), >0.175 CPU/system-bound, between -> ambiguous. Plausibility guard demotes wrong-process captures to Tier 2.

nodes.label: FPS Cap Gate (runs before busy-ratio logic)
nodes.rationale: Under an FPS cap, CPU Busy ~= frametime even when the CPU idles (verified in sample: 120 cap, CPU Busy 8.03ms vs frametime 8.33ms), so a capped window is classified 'capped' and busy-ratio logic is suppressed.
nodes.norm_label: fps cap gate (runs before busy-ratio logic)

nodes.label: Time-Split + Worst-Moments Verdict
nodes.rationale: The verdict speaks from the per-window time split ('GPU-bound 71% of gameplay') with the headline naming the dominant limiter, plus forensics on the worst FPS-drop windows showing time-aligned sensor state.

nodes.label: Never-Assert List
nodes.rationale: Five claims HWiNFO cannot evidence (background-process attribution, RAM latency-boundness, shader-comp vs streaming stutter, sub-window stutter without per-frame data, CPU-vs-GPU bound under a cap) are never asserted; a guidance catalog phrases them as 'can't measure this — here's what would'.

nodes.label: Root-Cause Analyzers (src/causes/)
nodes.rationale: Evidence-graded analyzers (cpuBound, gpuBound, thermalCollapse, vramPressure, ramPressure, fpsCap, hotspotDelta) consuming WindowAnalysis; replaces the whole-log heuristic src/detect/ layer.

nodes.label: buildGuidance Missing-Sensor Checklist
nodes.rationale: verdict/guidance.ts builds the 'what to enable for a sharper verdict' checklist (PresentMon, framerate source, polling rate, per-core sensors) ordered by impact; empty when the log is fully instrumented.

nodes.label: Warn-but-Allow Mismatch Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Mismatched runs (machine, FPS source, duration) warn but still compute the diff. HWiNFO logs carry no game/scene identity, so a fixed 'confirm both runs were the same workload' caveat is always appended.

nodes.label: buildCompareDigest (stacked BEFORE/AFTER digest)
nodes.rationale: Stacks both runs' stored digests labeled BEFORE/AFTER under a generated delta-summary block with a compare-aware goal line; never includes raw CSV.

nodes.label: SlimResult Persisted Run Form
nodes.rationale: The spec's ~15 KB-per-run assumption is false post-v1.5: real AnalysisResults serialize to megabytes (row-aligned arrays, cores matrix, windows), so 20 full runs cannot fit the ~5 MB localStorage quota. slimResult() strips every row-aligned array, keeping stats/events/verdict/digest/time-split/worst; a test pins a 2000-row log at <=~40 KB.

nodes.label: runsStore (wtfps.runs.v1, 20-run FIFO)
nodes.rationale: Persists SavedRun[] under wtfps.runs.v1 with a 20-run FIFO cap and auto-name '<GPU model> — HH:MM', mirroring specsStore's swallow-on-quota posture.

nodes.label: compareRuns Diff Engine
nodes.rationale: Pure diff over two SlimResults: sensor/hero deltas with polarity, event diff, mismatch detection, plain-language headline. Hero deltas computed from stats following buildVerdict's fallback chains — never parsed back out of display strings.

nodes.label: Delta Polarity Table
nodes.rationale: Lower-better: temps, power, RAM/pagefile, frame times, flag fired-counts. Higher-better: FPS avg + lows. Neutral (delta shown, no color): usages, clocks, voltages, fans, VRAM MB — ambiguous metrics never get a good/bad color.

nodes.label: Event Diff (resolved/introduced/persisted)
nodes.rationale: Events matched across runs keyed on type:subtype (DiagEvent gains optional subtype, e.g. 'gpu-thermal') so 'CPU throttling resolved' is distinguishable from 'GPU throttling introduced'.

nodes.label: RunsPanel Modal
nodes.rationale: Modal listing saved runs: rename, delete, clear-all, reopen as read-only SavedRunView, select two to compare.

nodes.label: Explicit Save Run Button
nodes.rationale: Saving becomes an explicit choice: the auto-save effect is removed and a subtle-variant 'Save run' button is added (not accent — the page's single accent CTA is Copy prompt). Quota failure returns null and leaves the button retryable; after success it becomes a disabled 'Saved' state.

nodes.label: Saved-State via Object Identity
nodes.rationale: saved = (savedResult === result): a new analysis produces a new result object, so the Save button resets to unsaved automatically without extra bookkeeping.

nodes.label: Interactive uPlot Timeline
nodes.rationale: Nerd-only: FPS line + one curated sensor overlay with per-unit named scales, limiter/throttle rail and markers painted into the same canvas (one paint surface, no SVG/canvas scroll-sync bugs). Replaces the static SVG WindowTimeline outright.

nodes.label: computeSelection Brush Analysis
nodes.rationale: Pure engine function over a brushed row range: rows are the engine's native coordinate, converted once at the chart boundary; time split reuses existing window classifications (windows fully inside the range) — no re-classification. Verdict and digest stay whole-log by user decision.

nodes.label: readChartTheme Token-to-Canvas Reader
nodes.rationale: CSS variables don't resolve inside a canvas, so JS reads theme tokens via getComputedStyle at mount instead of restating hex values — the DESIGN.md-compliant pattern.

nodes.label: Event-Marker Contract (windowIndexes)
nodes.rationale: The timeline paints a marker for every DiagEvent with non-empty windowIndexes and severity !== 'info', at the first listed window's center, colored by severity token; buildEventMarkers is the named seam plan #3 extends.

nodes.label: framePacing Micro-Stutter Analyzer
nodes.rationale: HWiNFO frame-time columns are per-poll averages of many frames, not per-frame data — surviving variability is real and understated, so sentences must say 'sampled frame-time variability'; tier measured with the polling caveat in evidence.basis. Skipped for workload (no-FPS) logs.

nodes.label: fanCurve Unresponsive-Fan Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Fires only when temps rise >=10C while the fan stays flat AND below 90% of its own session max — the only confident call is when the log itself shows the fan can spin faster; fan at max means cooling maxed, not a bad curve, so no event.

nodes.label: storageStutter Co-Location Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Frame-time spike clusters co-located with drive activity bursts; co-location is correlation, not causation, so evidence tier is 'inferred' and the basis says so. Absolute floors (activity >=10%, read >=50 MB/s) guard the relative gates against near-idle drives.

nodes.label: Shared Pacing Math (causes/pacing.ts)
nodes.rationale: Pure stutter primitives: gameplayRowSet (menus/loading legitimately spike and must be excluded), stutterIndex = p99/avg, spikeClusters, rowsToWindowIndexes; all-null/thin-data safe below 20 samples.

nodes.label: Multi-Instance Max Merge (multi: 'max')
nodes.rationale: A log can carry several drives/VRM rails; for keys marked multi:'max', normalize folds ALL matching columns into one per-row max series — the worst instance is the signal. Non-marked keys keep first-claim-wins untouched.

nodes.label: Golden No-False-Positive Guardrail
nodes.rationale: Goldens assert NO stutter/fan-curve/storage-stutter event fires on the 11 clean benchmark samples — a stutter call on a fixed-scene benchmark is a false positive by definition. If one fires, tune the gates and document it; never delete the assertion.

nodes.label: Alias-First Registry Breadth
nodes.rationale: New hardware support is overwhelmingly a naming problem, not semantics: almost every new label (desktop Ryzen, Radeon, Arc) maps onto an existing CanonicalKey so downstream gets new hardware for free. Every alias carries provenance; unverified aliases are marked provisional. Only one new key: gpu.socTempC.

nodes.label: parseReport (HWiNFO Save Report Parser)
nodes.rationale: Handles TXT and HTM report formats with no DOM (regex tag-strip keeps it node-testable and worker-safe); extracts only fields the report states outright; the report must never remove knowledge — vendor flags and laptop detection stay with the CSV fingerprint. Returns null on garbage, never throws.

nodes.label: mergeSpecs (report-wins merge)
nodes.rationale: Every non-null report field overwrites; everything else preserved byte-for-byte. Kept separate from parseReport so the merge rule is independently testable and reusable.

nodes.label: tempRanges Class-Level Reference DB
nodes.rationale: Expected temp ranges at vendor x laptop/desktop granularity — a per-SKU table would rot instantly and add nothing the class doesn't say. Unknown vendors fall back to the current hardcoded thresholds so behavior only changes where more is actually known; every entry's note cites its basis.

nodes.label: Profile-Parameterized Digest Renderer
nodes.rationale: One render() function parameterized by DigestProfile (detailed/terse/forum) — forking it per profile would triple the byte-compat surface. Flags are named after the digest's actual blocks; always-rendered blocks stay unconditional in every profile.

nodes.label: Goal Presets (GOAL_PRESETS chips)
nodes.rationale: Presets are data, not logic: five chips (lower temps / more FPS / fix stutter / quieter fans / diagnose a crash); the first equals DEFAULT_GOAL so one chip starts active; the crash preset points the LLM at the end of the log.

nodes.label: Self-Contained HTML Report Card
nodes.rationale: HTML in, PNG out: a DOM-screenshot PNG needs an html2canvas-class dependency (~150 KB) in a zero-dependency-pride app, fights CORS/canvas-taint, and duplicates an OS screenshot. The self-contained HTML (no scripts, no external URLs) keeps selectable text and zero deps; colors/fonts are snapshotted from live theme.css tokens at export time so theme.css stays the single source of truth.

nodes.label: Byte-for-Byte Back-Compat Pins
nodes.rationale: Before any refactor, the current compact and full digest output is frozen as inline snapshots (deliberately deviating from fail-first TDD) so the profile refactor cannot drift a byte; the detailed profile must reproduce today's full output exactly.

nodes.label: PWA Precache-Everything Offline Strategy
nodes.rationale: vite-plugin-pwa generateSW over hand-rolling because keeping the precache manifest in sync with Vite's hashed filenames is the error-prone part. The app makes zero runtime network calls, so precaching everything IS the offline strategy — runtime caching routes would be dead code. registerType 'prompt': never auto-swap code under a user mid-analysis.

nodes.label: useModal Focus-Trap Hook
nodes.rationale: Centralizes dialog focus behavior (focus-in on open, Tab/Shift-Tab cycle, Escape closes, focus restores to opener) for the settings overlay and RunsPanel, replacing ad-hoc handlers.

nodes.label: vitest-axe Smoke Suite
nodes.rationale: Axe runs over Landing and both Results modes with the color-contrast rule disabled — contrast needs real layout/canvas and is unreliable in jsdom, so it's covered by a manual DevTools audit in the committed checklist instead. PWA correctness is inherently manual: a service worker never runs inside Vitest.

nodes.label: PwaToast Offline/Update Toast
nodes.rationale: Always-mounted polite live region (mounted before content so screen readers announce insertions): 'Ready to work offline' auto-dismisses; 'Update available' offers an explicit Reload — no silent mid-session swap.

nodes.label: Shared Mascot/Icon Language
nodes.rationale: The in-app mascot and the app icon should read as the same character: 'icon face on the monitor body' for the mascot, 'the tile is the head' for the icon — big white oval eyes with tinted pupils and a waveform mouth, bold at 16-32 px favicon sizes.

nodes.label: FPS-Waveform Mouth
nodes.rationale: The mouth is an FPS trace whose shape tells the story per mood: healthy spike (chill), frame-drop dip (concerned), crash (panic); it tints with mood while the orange 'frame drop' dot stays #ff7a18 in every mood.

nodes.label: WTFPS App Icon (robot mascot face with FPS-waveform mouth)
nodes.norm_label: wtfps app icon (robot mascot face with fps-waveform mouth)

nodes.label: Mascot face language (big white oval eyes, tinted pupils, eye-shine, antenna)
nodes.rationale: The 2026-06-11 mascot-icon restyle made the app icon and the in-app mascot (src/ui/Mascot.tsx) read as the same character: the icon tile IS the robot's head. Shared traits: two large white ellipse eyes, accent-blue (#3b9eff) pupils with white eye-shine highlights, and an antenna dot above the head.
nodes.norm_label: mascot face language (big white oval eyes, tinted pupils, eye-shine, antenna)

nodes.label: FPS-waveform mouth with orange frame-drop dot
nodes.rationale: The mascot's mouth is drawn as a frametime/FPS line graph (accent-blue polyline) whose sharpest spike is marked by an orange dot (#ff7a18, a brand orange not present in theme.css tokens) representing a frame drop. This encodes the app's purpose - diagnosing FPS drops from HWiNFO logs - directly into the brand mark.
nodes.norm_label: fps-waveform mouth with orange frame-drop dot

nodes.label: Accent color token --accent (#3b9eff)
nodes.rationale: Design contract allows exactly one accent color across the UI; the app icon hardcodes the same hex so the brand mark and UI share an identity.
